cause_plain: The app wouldn't start. A route is set to return 204 No Content, but FastAPI also treated the function's return type (for example `-> None` or a dict) as a response body. It refused to register the route.
real_cause: get_typed_annotation() turned the string annotation 'None' (from postponed annotations) into NoneType rather than None, so the route was treated as having a response body and the 204 assertion failed.

cause_plain: Building a link fails with a TypeError if the link has a URL value named "self". Flask treats that name as its own internal argument instead of passing it on as a URL value.
real_cause: Flask.url_for() declared self as an ordinary parameter, so a URL value named 'self' passed via **values collided with it; the fix makes self positional-only.

cause_plain: A POST with a plain text body failed. The client announced a body length, but never actually sent the body, so the request broke and the user got a confusing protocol error instead of a response.
real_cause: RedirectMiddleware.redirect_headers() kept Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding when a redirect switched the method to GET and dropped the body, so h11 saw too little data for the declared length.

cause_plain: Decorating a class that defines an `__attrs_pre_init__` method with `@define` crashes at import time. attrs builds the class's `__init__` as generated Python code, and that code is not valid, so Python rejects it with a SyntaxError.
real_cause: _attrs_to_init_script() built the __attrs_pre_init__ call from kw_only argument strings that still included '=default', generating invalid code like a=attr_dict['a'].default=a=....

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a file that has a multiline (triple-quoted) string. It checked whether a line is short enough and hit a code token that had never been given its nesting-depth number.
real_cause: blib2to3 Leaf declared bracket_depth only as an annotation and neither __init__ nor clone() set it, so leaves created outside the bracket tracker lacked the attribute that is_line_short_enough() reads.
